title: "merge2023and2024"
author: "Noah Thomas"
date: "2026-09-12"
output: pdf_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

load in required libraries
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyverse)
library(openxlsx)
```

we read in the data we received below for both years
```{r}
chem2023 = read.csv("2023ver2.csv", header = TRUE)
chem2024 = read.csv("2024ver2.csv", header = TRUE)
```

Our objective in this file is to merge the 2023 and 2024 data that includes all info for both years for general use. I also perform some very general cleaning. 

Before we merge, we have to do general cleaning of both dataframes, since they won't be combined if columns have different data types. we do this below
```{r}
#NAs are removed here and replaced with 0s. Since these features acted binary, this just makes analysis easier
chem2024 = chem2024 %>%
  mutate(across(c(StudyGroupsYN.Registered.Sep9, StudyGroupsYN.Waitlisted.Sep9, TutoringYN.Sep9, Workshop_1.Sun, Workshop_1.Mon, Workshop_3.Sun, Workshop_3.Mon), ~ ifelse(is.na(.), 0, 1)))

chem2023 = chem2023 %>%
  mutate(across(c(Workshop_3.Sun, Workshop_3.Mon, Workshop_2.Sun, Workshop_2.Mon), ~ ifelse(is.na(.), 0, 1)))
#We make sure the features that are supposed to purely numeric are like so. This code turns any entries that werent numbers into NAs
chem2024 = chem2024 %>%
mutate(Exam2.Score_raw = as.numeric(Exam2.Score_raw),
       Exam3.Score_raw = as.numeric(Exam3.Score_raw),
       ExamFinal.Score_raw = as.numeric(ExamFinal.Score_raw),
       Homework.Achieve = as.numeric(Homework.Achieve),
       Exam2.Diff_to_instr.median = as.numeric(Exam2.Diff_to_instr.median),
       Exam3.Diff_to_instr.median = as.numeric(Exam3.Diff_to_instr.median),
       ExamFinal.Diff_to_instr.median = as.numeric(ExamFinal.Diff_to_instr.median),
       Grade.Final.. = as.numeric(Grade.Final..))

chem2023 = chem2023 %>%
mutate(Exam2.Score_raw = as.numeric(Exam2.Score_raw),
       Exam3.Score_raw = as.numeric(Exam3.Score_raw),
       ExamFinal.Score_raw = as.numeric(ExamFinal.Score_raw),
       Homework.Achieve = as.numeric(Homework.Achieve),
       Exam2.Diff_to_instr.median = as.numeric(Exam2.Diff_to_instr.median),
       Exam3.Diff_to_instr.median = as.numeric(Exam3.Diff_to_instr.median),
       ExamFinal.Diff_to_instr.median = as.numeric(ExamFinal.Diff_to_instr.median),
       Grade.Final.. = as.numeric(Grade.Final..))

#We rename these columns so they are matching for the 2023 and 2024 datasets. this makes the merge possible
chem2024 <- chem2024 %>% 
  rename(Engagement.faculty = Engagement_faculty)
```
now we merge
```{r}
mergedf = bind_rows(chem2023, chem2024)
```

Since we have done general cleaning and merged both spreadsheets, we are done. We export this csv so it can be uploaded
```{r}
write.xlsx(mergedf, "2023merged2024X.xlsx")
getwd()
```
